claims.claim: The SBA advises prospective businesses to identify startup expenses, estimate them, and organize them into one-time and monthly categories; applicable examples vary by business type.

A startup-cost checklist can include categories such as space, equipment, communications, utilities, licenses and permits, insurance, professional services, inventory, pay, marketing, market research, and a website, but no generic list applies to every venture.

Fixed and variable classify different cost behavior: over a stated relevant period, a fixed total does not change directly with activity, while a variable total changes with an activity driver; some costs combine both features.
The one-time-versus-recurring classification concerns payment timing and should not be treated as identical to the fixed-versus-variable classification.
Understanding cash needs requires attention to when expenses are due as well as their combined amount; cash-flow planning commonly records when cash arrives and when expenses are paid.
The lesson's $1,780 example is hypothetical and arithmetically equals $180 + $420 + $250 + $150 + 2 × ($240 + $90 + $60).
